title: Prove optimal weighted borrowed-source pair tours (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with exact finite corroboration, answering Cinna Davis's PR #2271 Open next question 2. For every n>=2 and positive toggle prices sorted c1>=...>=cn, the minimum closed borrowed-anchor tour through every pair mask is

```text
minimum transitions = 2*c1 + 2*sum_(i=2)^n (i-1)*ci
visit {1,n},...,{1,2}; {2,n},...,{2,3}; ...; {n-1,n}
write each assigned dirty target at its mask; restore the anchor
```

The forest lower bound permits arbitrary intermediate masks and repeated visits. For four toggle sources and two targets per pair, the complete restored-source map costs **26 row ADDs instead of 36 direct ADDs**, saving ten. Prices (7,3,2,1) have exact transition optimum 34. The new theorem, constructor, proof and independent finite oracles are produced by Nick Petalas. Cinna Davis retains the borrowed-source interface, transition-sharing example and open-question credit.

## Evidence

- Before: direct independent source writes emit 36 ADDs for the four-source/twelve-target map. After: the emitted tour has 14 toggles and 12 writes, totaling 26. Both complete maps are checked on exact basis columns; the new circuit is also checked on all 131072 dirty states of that 17-row instance.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized verification pass: 121 permutation optima, 117 literal hypercube optima, 189 larger tours, 630 circuit basis columns, 132128 complete dirty states and 168 wide-row fixtures. Thirteen invalid inputs, four tour corruptions, three circuit corruptions and one legal expensive order exercise the boundaries.
- Each registered check takes about 1.2 seconds locally, far below its 120-second bound. The final registered hook completes in 2.78 seconds. Metadata/provenance pins, committed bytes and source history pass. Generated normal/optimized source-bound receipts agree; an isolated Git-free optimized replay passes. A separate read-only proof/code review found no blocker. No independent human or formal proof-kernel review is claimed.

Exact reproduction from the repository root, CPython 3.12 and standard library only:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/weighted-pair-mask-tour
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -B research/weighted-pair-mask-tour/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -O -B research/weighted-pair-mask-tour/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/weighted-pair-mask-tour --check-source-history
```

Expected direct status: `PASS_WEIGHTED_PAIR_MASK_TOUR`. Replace the interpreter prefix with a local CPython 3.12 installation elsewhere.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The alphabet permits only anchor toggles from unchanged sources and one anchor write per target. This is an optimum within that class, not an unrestricted CNOT minimum. The all-n real-price theorem is a written proof; the executable supports exact rational prices, 2–64 sources and a uniform 1–8 targets per pair. Native frames, actual caller occurrence, hosting, tape movement and recursive billing remain external. No predecessor executable, full selected cold replay, Lean or Docker run was performed. No supplier admission, complete multiplication theorem, new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

The `bit-helper-contract` card explicitly changes scope from R439 H2/K to this local row-register side result. Canonical base is `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`; the source README and catalogue are provenance pins. The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19134289), live open PRs/claims, merged-term searches and main README object/formula searches were checked before publication. Sparse local notes and unpublished work remain overlap limits.

## Related open work

- [#3891](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3891) prepares and restores one fixed helper response; this result optimizes transitions across the complete varying pair family. Its R439 interface is not imported or rechecked.
- [#1865](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1865) groups exactly commuting complex fanout intervals; this proof concerns binary source-mask tours and makes no physical profile comparison.
- [#4891](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4891) lower-bounds dense dirty-output bank scans under monomial maps; this result prices one-anchor scalar row ADDs with specified pair demands. No predecessor numbers are recomputed for comparison.

- [#4896](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4896) determines dirty-root stock for a fixed repeated source order serving every nonzero mask; this result fixes one borrowed anchor and optimizes weighted transitions through pair masks. Root stock and tour cost are different quantities, and no numerical comparison is inferred.
- [#4894](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4894) studies within-class pair-sum excess on simple binary prefix walks; this result concerns the cost of visiting a prescribed complete pair-mask family and allows repeated walk states. Its census and bounds are not replayed here.

## Open next questions

- Locate an actual aligned caller demanding these pair parities at one cut, then price its frames, references, restoration, storage and tape movement.
- For an actual caller needing only a subset of pairs, determine its weighted tour optimum. The complete-pair forest bound need not remain sharp.
